prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: rear-end collision in League City, Texas. Injury: wrist fracture. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1354; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, if that's okay. You can use the case caption.

Q: That's fine. Where were you on the day of the collision?

A: I was driving home from work, heading south on a main road in League City, Texas. Traffic had slowed for a light ahead of me.

Q: Walk me through what happened right before the impact.

A: I came to a stop behind a sedan at the light. I had my foot on the brake and I was looking at the signal. The next thing I knew, I felt a hard jolt from behind and my head snapped forward.

Q: Did you see the vehicle that hit you?

A: Only in the mirror, just before. It was a pickup truck, and it looked like it wasn't slowing down.

Q: After the collision, what did you do?

A: I sat there for a moment. My right hand was pressed against the steering wheel and the pain shot up my arm almost immediately. I got out, checked on the driver ahead of me, and then called the police.

Q: When did you first seek medical care?

A: That evening. My wrist was swelling and I couldn't close my hand. A friend drove me to an urgent care clinic, and they sent me for X-rays the next day.

Q: What did the imaging show?

A: A fracture in the wrist, on the right side. The doctor explained that it was a break near the end of the radius bone.

Q: What treatment did you receive?

A: They put me in a cast for about six weeks. Then I went to physical therapy twice a week for several months to regain grip strength and range of motion.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?

A: Pretty significantly. I'm right-handed, so simple things like buttoning a shirt, cooking, or typing for long stretches were hard for a long time. I had to hire someone to help with yard work, and I stopped playing the weekly tennis league I'd been in for years.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Some. When the weather turns cold, my wrist aches and I lose grip strength by the end of the day. I still do my home exercises most mornings.

Q: Thank you. Nothing further at this time.
